"""Figure 1: Differential Depth Response — redesigned as strip/forest plot.
Wong colorblind-safe palette, diamond grand means, per-generator dots."""
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
import numpy as np
import json

# ── Data ──
with open('/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0514_3/projects/gen-depth-fingerprint/artifacts/_project/rebuttal/spearman_per_generator.json') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

features = [
    ('hapax_ratio',   r'Hapax ratio',                      'drifting',     0.76),
    ('ttr',           r'TTR',                               'drifting',     0.88),
    ('entropy_mean',  r'$\bar{H}$ (entropy mean)',          'drifting',     1.17),
    ('entropy_min',   r'$H_{\min}$ (entropy min)',          'near-stat',    0.016),
    ('entropy_std',   r'$\sigma_H$ (entropy std)',          'intermediate', 0.55),
    ('entropy_max',   r'$H_{\max}$ (entropy max)',          'near-stat',    0.08),
    ('tail_decay',    r'Tail decay',                        'near-stat',    0.08),
]

generators = list(data.keys())
gen_short = ['Py-1B', 'Py-2.8B', 'OLMo', 'Qw-0.6B', 'Qw-1.7B', 'Qw-8B', 'Llama', 'Mistral']

# ── Style ── (Wong colorblind-safe from Nature Methods)
C_DRIFT  = '#0072B2'   # blue
C_INTERM = '#882255'   # wine/mauve (Tol palette)
C_STAT   = '#E69F00'   # amber
C_BG_DRIFT  = '#0072B2'
C_BG_INTERM = '#882255'
C_BG_STAT   = '#E69F00'

zone_color = {'drifting': C_DRIFT, 'intermediate': C_INTERM, 'near-stat': C_STAT}

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['DejaVu Serif'],
    'font.size': 8,
    'axes.labelsize': 9,
    'xtick.labelsize': 7.5,
    'ytick.labelsize': 8,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.04,
    'mathtext.fontset': 'cm',
})

n = len(features)
y_pos = np.arange(n)[::-1]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(3.25, 2.6))

# ── Zone background shading ──
zone_ranges = {
    'drifting':     (y_pos[2] - 0.42, y_pos[0] + 0.42),
    'intermediate': (y_pos[4] - 0.42, y_pos[4] + 0.42),
    'near-stat':    (y_pos[6] - 0.42, y_pos[3] + 0.42),
}
for zone, (ylo, yhi) in zone_ranges.items():
    ax.axhspan(ylo, yhi, color=zone_color[zone], alpha=0.04, zorder=0)

# ── Separator lines between zones ──
sep1 = (y_pos[2] + y_pos[3]) / 2
sep2 = (y_pos[4] + y_pos[3]) / 2
ax.axhline(sep1, color='#cccccc', linewidth=0.5, linestyle='-', zorder=1)
ax.axhline(sep2, color='#cccccc', linewidth=0.5, linestyle='-', zorder=1)

# ── Zero line ──
ax.axvline(0, color='#bbbbbb', linewidth=0.6, linestyle='-', zorder=1)

# ── Per-generator dots + grand mean diamond ──
gen_markers = ['o', 's', '^', 'D', 'v', 'P', 'X', '*']
np.random.seed(42)

for i, (feat_key, label, zone, d_val) in enumerate(features):
    yi = y_pos[i]
    c = zone_color[zone]

    vals = [data[g][feat_key] for g in generators]
    grand_mean = np.mean(vals)

    jitter = np.linspace(-0.18, 0.18, len(vals))

    for j, (v, gm) in enumerate(zip(vals, gen_markers)):
        ax.scatter(v, yi + jitter[j], marker='o', s=14,
                   color=c, alpha=0.45, edgecolors='none', zorder=3,
                   linewidths=0)

    # Grand mean: diamond marker with white edge
    ax.scatter(grand_mean, yi, marker='D', s=50, color=c,
               edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.8, zorder=5)

    # Thin connecting line from min to max (range)
    ax.plot([min(vals), max(vals)], [yi, yi],
            color=c, linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.35, zorder=2, solid_capstyle='round')

# ── Y-axis labels ──
ax.set_yticks(y_pos)
ax.set_yticklabels([f[1] for f in features], fontsize=7)

# ── X-axis ──
ax.set_xlabel(r'Spearman $\rho$ with generation depth', fontsize=8)
ax.set_xlim(-0.82, 0.22)
ax.set_ylim(-0.55, n - 0.45)

# ── Axis styling ──
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['left'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('#999999')
ax.spines['bottom'].set_linewidth(0.5)
ax.tick_params(axis='y', length=0)
ax.tick_params(axis='x', length=3, width=0.5, color='#999999')

# ── Zone labels on right margin ──
zone_info = [
    ('drifting',     (y_pos[0] + y_pos[2]) / 2,  'Drifting',         r'$d = 0.76$–$1.17$'),
    ('intermediate', y_pos[4],                     'Intermediate',     r'$d = 0.55$'),
    ('near-stat',    (y_pos[3] + y_pos[6]) / 2,   'Near-stationary',  r'$d < 0.10$'),
]
for zone, ym, lbl, sub in zone_info:
    ax.text(0.20, ym + 0.13, lbl, fontsize=5.5, color=zone_color[zone],
            fontweight='bold', va='bottom', ha='right', style='italic')
    ax.text(0.20, ym - 0.13, sub, fontsize=5, color=zone_color[zone],
            va='top', ha='right')

# ── Legend ──
legend_elements = [
    plt.scatter([], [], marker='o', s=14, color='#666', alpha=0.5,
                edgecolors='none', label='Per-generator'),
    plt.scatter([], [], marker='D', s=50, color='#666',
                edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.8, label='Grand mean'),
]
leg = ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='lower left',
                fontsize=5.5, frameon=True, framealpha=0.9,
                edgecolor='#dddddd', fancybox=False,
                handletextpad=0.3, borderpad=0.4,
                bbox_to_anchor=(0.0, 0.0))
leg.get_frame().set_linewidth(0.4)

plt.tight_layout()

out = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0514_3/projects/gen-depth-fingerprint/artifacts/_project/chart'
fig.savefig(f'{out}/fig1_differential_response.pdf', format='pdf')
fig.savefig(f'{out}/fig1_differential_response.png', format='png')
print(f'Saved to {out}/')

\paragraph{Cross-model generalization.}
Cross-model chains (randomly selected generator per step) provide an exploratory evaluation of depth signal under generator heterogeneity, yielding binary F1\,=\,0.830 (95\% CI [.818, .841]) under generator-level leave-one-out evaluation on the 5-generator subset for which cross-model chains were available (Pythia-2.8B/1B, OLMo-2-1B, Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B).\footnote{We corrected the cross-model chain evaluation from sample-level CV to generator-level LOGO for consistency with our main evaluation protocol. CIs are case-level bootstrap ($n$\,=\,2{,}000). The 5-generator result is not directly comparable to the 8-generator LOGO (binary F1\,=\,0.694) due to differing generator subsets.}
The higher cross-model binary F1 relative to the 8-generator LOGO (0.694) is not directly comparable: the cross-model evaluation uses a 5-generator subset, and generator heterogeneity in mixed chains may amplify depth-correlated distributional shifts.
A single-generator transfer analysis (Appendix~\ref{app:transfer}) provides evidence against this confound: classifiers trained on one generator transfer to all seven others with mean binary F1\,=\,0.810 (95\% CI [0.796, 0.822]), significantly above chance.
Leave-one-family-out (LOFO) evaluation yields binary F1\,=\,0.686, consistent with cross-family transfer.
A scale effect emerges: Pythia generators achieve the highest binary F1 (0.718--0.724), while larger models show degradation (Mistral-7B: 0.633), partly reflecting same-family affinity with the Pythia-410M reference model (cross-reference spread $\leq$0.013; \S\ref{sec:results-differential}).
Preliminary cross-domain evaluation suggests the signal persists with variation, though a domain$\times$temperature interaction exists (Appendix~\ref{app:domain}).
An end-to-end QLoRA classifier achieves 3-class F1\,=\,0.905 (6-generator LOGO; $+$11.6\,pp; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}), which indicates that richer representations capture additional depth signal beyond the 7-feature set; on instruct data, QLoRA recovers to 0.89--0.91 (Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}).
The consistent QLoRA improvement ($+$11.6\,pp under matched LOGO) confirms that DDR's primary contribution is the empirical decomposition, not the specific classifier.

DDR connects to but is mechanistically distinct from model collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion,strong_model_collapse}.
Both phenomena manifest as distributional compression under iterative processing, and DDR's drifting features (entropy mean, TTR, hapax ratio) capture the same lexical diversity loss documented as ``diversity collapse'' in retraining studies \cite{strong_model_collapse}.
The critical distinction is between parameter-level and activation-level compression: retraining permanently erodes tail coverage by updating model weights, whereas inference-chain drift at fixed parameters shifts only the location of the NLL distribution, leaving its shape as a stable reference.
Prior analyses of iterative generation document that \emph{something} converges---diversity loss \cite{curious_decline}, attractor dynamics \cite{markovian_chains}, mode collapse \cite{curse_of_recursion}---but not what is \emph{preserved}.
DDR's contribution is this complementary observation: shape features remain invariant under the same process that compresses location, and this asymmetry is precisely what enables depth detection without per-generator calibration.
Three depth classes represent the practical resolution ceiling (5-class F1\,$\approx$\,0.50; Appendix~\ref{app:finer-depth}), though richer representations recover substantially more signal (QLoRA F1\,=\,0.905; Appendix~\ref{app:qlora}).
Instruction-tuned models show attenuated fingerprints (OLMo-Instruct LOGO F1\,=\,0.338 vs.\ 0.763 base) with reversed feature correlations, suggesting alignment reshapes the generation attractor rather than eliminating depth signal; QLoRA recovers to F1\,=\,0.89--0.91 on instruct data (Appendix~\ref{app:instruct}), confirming token-level signal persists despite summary-statistic degradation.

\paragraph{Feature complementarity.}
The seven features were selected a priori from two complementary perspectives (reference-model NLL distribution and surface lexical diversity) to enable interpretable decomposition of depth signal; exploring richer feature spaces (syntactic complexity, semantic coherence) may improve classification but at the cost of the location/shape analysis that is the paper's primary contribution.

TTR and hapax ratio are strongly correlated ($r = 0.97$); both are retained for marginal LOFO gains.

"""Figure 1: DDR trajectory — 2×2 panel showing drifting vs stationary features.
Wong colorblind-safe palette, diamond grand means, per-generator thin lines."""
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

DATA = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0514_3/projects/gen-depth-fingerprint/artifacts/_project/supplement/data/features_all_models.csv'
df = pd.read_csv(DATA)

plt.rcParams.update({
    'font.family': 'serif',
    'font.serif': ['DejaVu Serif'],
    'font.size': 8,
    'axes.labelsize': 8,
    'xtick.labelsize': 7,
    'ytick.labelsize': 7,
    'figure.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.dpi': 300,
    'savefig.bbox': 'tight',
    'savefig.pad_inches': 0.04,
    'mathtext.fontset': 'cm',
})

# Wong colorblind-safe palette (8 colors)
PALETTE = [
    '#0072B2',  # blue  — Pythia-2.8B
    '#56B4E9',  # sky   — Pythia-1B
    '#009E73',  # green — OLMo
    '#E69F00',  # amber — Qwen-0.6B
    '#D55E00',  # vermillion — Qwen-1.7B
    '#CC79A7',  # pink  — Qwen-8B
    '#F0E442',  # yellow — Llama (darkened below)
    '#882255',  # wine  — Mistral
]

GENERATORS = [
    ('pythia-2.8b',      'Py-2.8B',   PALETTE[0]),
    ('pythia-1b',        'Py-1B',     PALETTE[1]),
    ('olmo-2-1b',        'OLMo',      PALETTE[2]),
    ('qwen3-0.6b',       'Qw-0.6B',   PALETTE[3]),
    ('qwen3-1.7b',       'Qw-1.7B',   PALETTE[4]),
    ('qwen3-8b',         'Qw-8B',     PALETTE[5]),
    ('llama-3.2-3b',     'Llama',     '#999900'),  # darkened yellow for visibility
    ('mistral-7b-v0.3',  'Mistral',   PALETTE[7]),
]

# Zone colors for grand mean
C_DRIFT = '#0072B2'
C_STAT  = '#E69F00'

features = [
    ('entropy_mean', r'Entropy Mean ($\bar{H}$)',  'drifting'),
    ('hapax_ratio',  r'Hapax Ratio',               'drifting'),
    ('entropy_max',  r'Entropy Max ($H_{\max}$)',   'stationary'),
    ('tail_decay',   r'Tail Decay',                 'stationary'),
]

depths = sorted(df['depth'].unique())

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(6.8, 4.0), sharex=True)
panel_labels = ['(a)', '(b)', '(c)', '(d)']

for idx, (feat, label, zone) in enumerate(features):
    ax = axes[idx // 2][idx % 2]
    c_mean = C_DRIFT if zone == 'drifting' else C_STAT

    all_means = []
    for gen_name, gen_short, gen_color in GENERATORS:
        sub = df[df['model_name'] == gen_name]
        means = sub.groupby('depth')[feat].mean().reindex(depths)
        all_means.append(means.values)
        ax.plot(depths, means.values,
                color=gen_color, linewidth=0.8, alpha=0.5,
                marker='o', markersize=2.5, markeredgewidth=0, zorder=2)

    grand = np.mean(all_means, axis=0)
    ax.plot(depths, grand,
            color=c_mean, linewidth=2.0, alpha=0.9, zorder=4)
    ax.scatter(depths, grand,
               color=c_mean, marker='D', s=35,
               edgecolors='white', linewidths=0.7, zorder=5)

    # Spearman rho annotation
    from scipy.stats import spearmanr
    all_depth_vals = []
    all_feat_vals = []
    for gen_name, _, _ in GENERATORS:
        sub = df[df['model_name'] == gen_name]
        all_depth_vals.extend(sub['depth'].values)
        all_feat_vals.extend(sub[feat].values)
    rho, _ = spearmanr(all_depth_vals, all_feat_vals)
    ax.text(0.97, 0.95, rf'$\rho = {rho:.3f}$',
            transform=ax.transAxes, fontsize=6.5,
            va='top', ha='right', color='#555',
            bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.2', facecolor='white',
                      edgecolor='#ddd', linewidth=0.4, alpha=0.9))

    ax.set_title(f'{panel_labels[idx]} {label}', fontsize=8, pad=4,
                 loc='left', fontweight='normal')

    ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines['left'].set_color('#999')
    ax.spines['left'].set_linewidth(0.5)
    ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('#999')
    ax.spines['bottom'].set_linewidth(0.5)
    ax.tick_params(length=3, width=0.5, color='#999')
    ax.set_xticks(depths)

    if idx >= 2:
        ax.set_xlabel('Generation Depth', fontsize=7.5)

# Row labels
for ax in axes[0]:
    ax.xaxis.set_tick_params(labelbottom=False)

# Legend: generators + grand mean
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D
handles = []
for _, gen_short, gen_color in GENERATORS:
    handles.append(Line2D([0], [0], color=gen_color, linewidth=0.8,
                          alpha=0.6, marker='o', markersize=2.5,
                          markeredgewidth=0, label=gen_short))
handles.append(Line2D([0], [0], color='#555', linewidth=0, marker='D',
                       markersize=5, markeredgecolor='white',
                       markeredgewidth=0.7, label='Grand Mean'))

fig.legend(handles=handles, loc='lower center', ncol=5,
           fontsize=5.5, frameon=True, framealpha=0.95,
           edgecolor='#ddd', fancybox=False,
           handletextpad=0.3, columnspacing=1.0,
           bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.02))

plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.06, 1, 1])
plt.subplots_adjust(hspace=0.25, wspace=0.28)

out = '/home/ubuntu/.agent-ml-research-idea_gen_0514_3/projects/gen-depth-fingerprint/artifacts/_project/chart'
fig.savefig(f'{out}/fig_ddr_trajectory.pdf', format='pdf')
fig.savefig(f'{out}/fig_ddr_trajectory.png', format='png')
print(f'Saved trajectory figure to {out}/')
